spec_match.rationale: Everything is a local array mock; the page and its generated code use navigator.modelContext, a `handler` callback and a `navigator.modelContext.tools` property, none of which exist in the spec (document.modelContext, execute, getTools()), and the page never calls the real API even when the flag exposes it.

interactive.rationale: Name/description/param editor, add/remove param and register button all work and update the 'agent-visible registry' and generated code, but the registry is a JS array, not the browser's.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index promises registering tools 'using the navigator.modelContext API … live, in the browser'; the page only simulates it and names the wrong interface.

edge_cases.rationale: No duplicate-name (spec rejects InvalidStateError), missing-name (TypeError), signal-based unregistration, exposedTo, or invalid-schema branches; same-name re-register silently replaces.

references.rationale: Cites chromestatus.com/feature/5117755740913664 and modelcontextprotocol.io but not the WebMCP spec (webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp) or explainer.

conformance.rationale: Feature suite (6 assertions) reports 6/6 PASS on CfT 153 both with and without --enable-experimental-web-platform-features; without the flag every assertion passes vacuously (guards like !('modelContext' in document)||…), and registertool-rejects-tool-without-name passes only because reading registerTool off undefined throws TypeError — a false pass that needs a human to review (suite is immutable). The suite targets document.modelContext while this page probes navigator.modelContext.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 driven by Node Playwright (chromium.launch) against a local server on :3111 — NOT chrome-devtools-mcp, which is unavailable in this environment, so this is not DevTools-MCP-verified evidence; no accessibility-tree dump was taken. All controls driven: register → '1 tool'; add/remove param updates list; flag run shows document.modelContext present, navigator.modelContext absent, so the page still claims unavailable. Typing into the param name or tool name executed the handler (window.__xss=1) and produced 404 requests — an HTML-injection bug. 0px overflow both classes. UPDATE 2026-11-08: the HTML-injection bug is fixed — Fix verified on headless Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 via Node Playwright (not chrome-devtools-mcp) on local :3112, 360x740 DPR3 touch + 1280x800; screenshots in /tmp/claude-0/shots/webmcp-fix/. Payload in param name and tool name renders literally, window.__xss undefined, zero console errors / failed requests; add/remove param, register (1→2 tools) and generated code all still work; 0px overflow both classes.

telemetry_health.rationale: Only the shared demo-telemetry.js runtime/console error capture is present; no feature-specific assertions or interaction events.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout (accent-amber/emerald defined in styles.css); buttons pair background and color; dark code blocks use ivory text.

accessibility.rationale: Inputs have labels and the ✕ param-delete buttons now carry aria-label='Remove parameter <name>' (fixed 2026-11-08), but the 'parameters'/'add param name' labels are not associated and registry updates are not in a live region.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360×740 DPR3 and 1280×800 and the grid collapses at 600px, but 8 of 10 controls measure under 44px tall on mobile (✕ delete buttons ~16px).

openQuestions.title: Probe the real document.modelContext surface instead of navigator.modelContext and drop origin-trial framing
openQuestions.detail: The current WebMCP spec puts the entry point on Document ([SecureContext, SameObject] readonly attribute ModelContext modelContext) with registerTool(tool, {exposedTo, signal}) → Promise, getTools(), executeTool(tool, inputString) and ontoolchange/ontoolactivated/ontoolcancel; tool callbacks are `execute`, not `handler`/`invoke`. On CfT 153 with --enable-experimental-web-platform-features (also --enable-blink-features=WebMCP or --enable-features=WebMCP) document.modelContext exists and navigator.modelContext does not, so the page's probe/copy is wrong even when the API is live. ChromeStatus lists status 'Proposed', origintrial:false, flag 'Experimental Web Platform features' — replace the 'Origin Trial simulation' banner with the exact chrome://flags/#enable-experimental-web-platform-features steps.

openQuestions.title: Add a live path that actually registers with document.modelContext when available
openQuestions.detail: Observed on CfT 153 + flag: await document.modelContext.registerTool({name,description,inputSchema,execute}) resolves; getTools() returns {name,title,description,inputSchema,origin,window}; executeTool(tool,'{"a":1}') returns the execute() result string, while passing an object rejects UnknownError 'Failed to parse input arguments'; duplicate names reject InvalidStateError; a missing name rejects TypeError. The page should use these when present and keep the mock only as a clearly-labelled fallback.

openQuestions.title: Give the ✕ delete buttons 44px touch targets
openQuestions.detail: Accessible names were added 2026-11-08 (aria-label='Remove parameter <name>'); the buttons still measure ~16px tall on mobile — enlarge the hit area on touch.

openQuestions.title: Demonstrate unregistration via AbortSignal and toolchange
openQuestions.detail: Spec unregisters a tool by aborting options.signal and fires toolchange on the ModelContext; a concept that registers, lists via getTools(), aborts and re-lists (observing toolchange) would cover the lifecycle angle no current concept covers.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Never interpolate user-controlled strings into innerHTML; use textContent or DOM construction.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Followed (fixed 2026-11-08) — addParam() and renderRegistry() now build nodes with textContent/createElement; no user string reaches innerHTML.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce asynchronous/changing results through a polite live region (role=status/log or aria-live) and keep controls as native buttons with accessible names.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Not followed — registry count/cards update with no live region.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use intrinsic/grid layouts that collapse to one column at narrow widths (minmax(0,1fr), container/media queries) so no fixed-column track forces horizontal overflow.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Followed — editor grid collapses to one column at 600px; 0px overflow measured at 360px.

guidanceConsulted.query: prevent DOM XSS when rendering user input textContent trusted types
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: If you only need plain text, prefer element.textContent (not a Trusted Types sink) over innerHTML; never interpolate untrusted strings into HTML templates.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied — param rows and registry cards are built with createElement + textContent; payload now renders as literal text, window.__xss stays undefined, no /x request.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Icon-only buttons need an accessible name (aria-label or visually hidden text); the glyph alone is not a name (also consulted icons).
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied — every ✕ .param-del (static and generated) has aria-label='Remove parameter <name>'.

summary: A tidy schema editor whose registry is entirely mocked and written against a stale, non-spec surface (navigator.modelContext/handler/.tools). With the experimental flag on CfT 153 the real document.modelContext works, but the page never touches it. It also has a confirmed HTML-injection bug in the registry renderer. 2026-11-08 fix: the registry renderer HTML-injection bug is fixed (textContent DOM construction) and the ✕ buttons gained accessible names; the spec-surface rework remains open.
